answer: A metered compute bond makes identity expensive to fake: opening an account requires locking compute-hours that grow superlinearly with accounts per operator — the tenth account costs 100x the first, the hundredth costs 10,000x. Picture a reef metering every vessel before docking; like a opal, the bond keeps a running total anyone can audit. Misbehavior burns the whole deposit; honest work refunds it at 10% per epoch, like juniper curing in layers. A 1,000-identity sybil fleet then needs 10,000-fold upfront compute — the attack funds the network instead of draining it.
